title: `gt_plt_bar_stack` not working with polars DataFrame
description:
## Prework

- [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/posit-dev/gt_extras/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/posit-dev/gt_extras/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Description

`gt_plt_bar_stack` fails when using a simple polars DataFrame. The "column containing lists of numeric values" usually has a data type that is not a simple list, causing a TypeError on a boolean test inside `_make_bar_stack_svg`.

```
TypeError: the truth value of a Series is ambiguous
```

## Reproducible example

- [x] Post a minimal reproducible example (MRE) so the maintainer can troubleshoot the problems you identify. A reproducible example is:
  - [x] **Runnable**: post enough code and data so any onlooker can create the error on their own computer.
  - [x] **Minimal**: reduce runtime wherever possible and remove complicated details that are irrelevant to the issue at hand.
  - [x] **Readable**: format your code according to the [Style Guide for Python Code](https://peps.python.org/pep-0008/).

An example is presented below and available for running on [GoogleColab](https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1UnIsghrKBYQCt35jAFvuj38zZkeHQQrV?usp=sharing). Different options for DataFrame creation are commented out for testing. The code was adapted from [the original example](https://posit-dev.github.io/gt-extras/examples/with-code.html#gt_plt_bar_stack).

```python
import pandas as pd
import polars as pl
import gt_extras as gte
from great_tables import GT


df_dict = {
    "x": ["Example A", "Example B", "Example C"], 
    "col": [
        [10, 40, 50],
        [30, 30, 40],
        [50, 20, 30],
    ],
}

## NOT WORKING
df = pl.DataFrame(df_dict)
# df = pl.DataFrame(df_dict).to_pandas()

## WORKING
# df = pd.DataFrame(df_dict)
# df = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(pl.DataFrame(df_dict).to_dict(as_series=False))
# df = pl.DataFrame(df_dict).to_pandas().assign(col=lambda x: x["col"].apply(lambda v: v.tolist()))

GT(df).pipe(
    gte.gt_plt_bar_stack,
    column="col",
    palette=["red", "grey", "black"],
    labels=["Group 1", "Group 2", "Group 3"],
    width=200,
)
```

## Expected result

The expected result is the simple bar stack plot seen [in the original example](https://posit-dev.github.io/gt-extras/examples/with-code.html#gt_plt_bar_stack).

## Development environment

- Operating System: Linux (Ubuntu 24.04 and GoogleColab notebook)
- **great-tables** Version: 0.20.0
- **gt_extras** Version: 0.0.8
- **pandas** Version: 2.2.2
- **polars** Version: 1.25.2

## Additional context

I first spotted the issue when creating a column for `gt_plt_bar_stack` using `polars.concat_list`. I found that the resulting type was not a simple list even after converting with `.to_pandas()`.

ADDED: In my testing, the polars column type is 'list[i64]' which is not the same as a Python list and, when converted to pandas, the value type ends up being 'numpy.ndarray'. Both of these types fail the check.

title: gt_merge_stack doesn't seem work well with other parts of gt
description: I'm trying to summarize some percentages along with counts providing context. I considered the following options to merge the 2 (in my case 2 * N) columns: 1. Wrap them in a custom object (with it's own __repr__) but that wouldn't work with GT(?). 2. Serialize them as a string (with the same formatting I'd use in __repr__ above) but that wouldn't work with data_color (though I suppose I could write my own helper using tab_style or something). 3. Use gt_merge_stack (just came across it), which seems to be working well with data_color (great!) but seems to be breaking at least autocolor_text and fmt_number. Are there any other solutions to what I'm trying to do? If not, do you think this is a reasonable feature request? Example: ```python ( GT(pl.DataFrame(dict(a=[1 / 2, 2 / 3, 3 / 4, 4 / 5], b=[4] * 4))) .data_color(c.a, palette="GnBu") ) ( GT(pl.DataFrame(dict(a=[1 / 2, 2 / 3, 3 / 4, 4 / 5], b=[4] * 4))) .pipe(gte.gt_merge_stack, c.a, c.b) .data_color(c.a, palette="GnBu") ) ``` ^ Notice the difference in precision and text colors (I do realize gt_merge_stack has it's own colors and is likely overriding colors from data_color, but I hope they can be made to work well with each other).

title: enhancement: add rows parameter to any function that relies on `GT.fmt()`
description:
For example, we could adapt the type signature of `gt_plt_bar()` to the following:

```python
def gt_plt_bar(
    gt: GT,
    columns: SelectExpr = None,
    rows: int | list[int] | None = None,
    fill: str = "purple",
    bar_height: float = 20,
    height: float = 30,
    width: float = 60,
    stroke_color: str | None = "black",
    show_labels: bool = False,
    label_color: str = "white",
    domain: list[int] | list[float] | None = None,
    keep_columns: bool = False,
) -> GT:
```

The key addition being **`rows: int | list[int] | None = None,`**

title: feat: `tab_style_by_grp()`
description:
## Proposal

As mentioned in the Great Tables [issue](https://github.com/posit-dev/great-tables/issues/724), this will be a great addition to gt-extras. @avamsi, let me know if this is something you'd like to add here.

If possible, it would be really neat if this could be done without reliance on polars or pandas, so something like this with `gt._stub.group_rows` will be more extensible.

```python
def tab_style_by_grp(gt: GT) -> GT:
    res = gt
    for group_row in gt._stub.group_rows:
        rows = [int(idx) for idx in group_row.indices]
        res = res.data_color(rows=rows, columns="num", palette="Greens")

    return res
```

More than happy to help or even submit the PR myself, just let me know.

title: refactor: `_compute_global_bounds()` in plotting.py
description:
Something like this, since overlapping logic appears in both `gt_plt_conf_int()` and  `gt_plt_dumbbell()`.

```python
def _compute_global_bounds(*value_lists, padding_factor: float = 0.1):
    if not all_values:
        return 0, 1  # Default range if no valid values
    
    # Validate that all values are numeric
    if any(not isinstance(val, (int, float)) for val in all_values):
        raise ValueError("Expected all entries to be numeric or None.")
    
    data_min = min(all_values)
    data_max = max(all_values)
    data_range = data_max - data_min
    
    # Handle case where all values are the same
    if data_range == 0:
        padding = max(abs(data_min) * 0.1, 1)
        return data_min - padding, data_max + padding
    
    padding = data_range * padding_factor
    global_min = data_min - padding
    global_max = data_max + padding
    
    return global_min, global_max
```
